body: @hguerrero could you prepare a small Maven reproducer? Thanks!

Here is a sample project.

If you retrieve /fruits/works (no call to page count) it works
If you request /fruits/fail crashes when trying to get the pageCount() as there the regex used is not correctly capturing the query.

[panache-projection.zip](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/files/4576130/panache-projection.zip)

OK, so it turns out that we were a bit optimistic when it came to generating count queries.

Initially I assumed all JPA queries started with "from X..." but then someone added support for "select distinct? foo from X", but only made it support a single column.

We do need to support the `distinct` use case because `select count(*)` will not lead to the same results as `select count(distinct name)`.

But after having checked the HQL grammar, select's `querySpec` clauses are just vastly more complicated.

@Sanne is there support do you think in Hibernate's API to turn a select query into a count query, or do I keep on supporting each use-case as bugs get reported until I go and use a proper HQL parser and do it entirely?

Also, this is not actually about paging, but about select clauses.

And also, it turns out I can't use a regex to match even the simple cases such as `select distinct? identifier (as identifier)?(, distinct? identifier (as identifier)?)*` because I'd need to drop the `as identifier` parts for `count`.

I just learned that it turns out `count(dinstinct? expression)` only takes a single expression.

So I simply don't know how to turn `select distinct a, b` into a count query.

> @Sanne is there support do you think in Hibernate's API to turn a select query into a count query, or do I keep on supporting each use-case as bugs get reported until I go and use a proper HQL parser and do it entirely?

I'm afraid there isn't; besides.. why do you need the count for paging? Attempting to return a list of total pages?

Such transformations might get far easier with ORM6; untile we update I wouldn't know of a clean solution for this.

@sebersole am I correct?

Correct about which?  

About questioning the whole idea of auto-magically doing paging counts?  I would agree about the dubiousness.

Or about it being easier or not with 6?  In theory having the semantic tree would make it easier to deduce the meaning and build an appropriate "select count" mutation.

> About questioning the whole idea of auto-magically doing paging counts? I would agree about the dubiousness.

Well, that's a feature a lot of people like, to be able to get a count of all results from a query so they can page it properly. So it's not like we have a choice in supporting it.

What we can do is figure out which queries are easy to generate a count for, and defer support for the others later.

But it looks like for now at least we're not getting help from the existing Hibernate API, too bad, it was worth a try :)

Thanks for checking, though.

I mean I'm not sure what kind of "help from the existing Hibernate API" you are looking for.  You mean some form of:

```
Query qry = ...;
final int count = qry.transformToCountQuery().getSingleResult();
```

?

Yeah, that's not going to happen.  Otherwise, make a suggestion

I was not really asking if you can make a new API, but if there already exists one that turns a query statement and turns it into a count statement. But yeah, ideally something that takes a `selectStatement` (in the words of the `HqlParser.g4` I copied from Hibernate 6) into one that returns a count query.

I figured perhaps with some luck you had that lying around somewhere in the API, but it's fairly possible you don't because you never need it.

If you don't have that, It'd be hard to justify adding it to Hibernate rather than me implementing it here.

From time to time, people do ask how to do the same on forums, etc.  So I guess I can see where people would find it useful.

Anyway, if we can do something to make it easier for you to do it we should consider it.  Is there anything that would make it easier for you?

@FroMage I have no doubts that "people would like to page properly" but I'm skeptical about us being able to automate it, without this becoming a significant project.

FYI in many databases the COUNT(*) query operation is very heavy, and takes approximately the same time as running the matching not-counting query.

The effect is extreme in some cases, to the point that for example in the MassIndexer of Hibernate Search when we had the count() approach in its first version - used to give people an approximate "progress bar" logged - this initial count was taking so long as the rest of indexing so the whole point of the progress bar was silly. Got rid of it, it's now twice as fast (it finishes in the same time it would start giving you a clue before).

Several DBs have low-acid alternatives which leverage statistics and lack of locking to give you a fairly accurate approximation; when I worked on systems needing a page count we'd hand-roll such SQL statements as it was much more effective; most importantly, we could toy with tradeoffs we knew were acceptable in our specific use case.

e.g. MySQL has `SELECT FOUND_ROWS();`, other databases have hints, I honestly don't remember how to do it the right way on each.

I'd say in some far future Hibernate ORM could have ad-hoc "dialect" support to know how to generate such things optimally on many databases, but until we get there I would suggest don't try this and let people write some native SQL.
